items.title: Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat Programme
items.explanation: The Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat programme is conducted to know that we all belong to one nation and share a bond. It aims to celebrate unity in diversity by enhancing interaction between people of different states or UTs through state/UT pairing.

items.title: Aipan Folk Art
items.explanation: Aipan is a folk art form made by women in families using white rice flour paste on brick-red walls coloured with geru. The designs are beautiful, mathematical, and based on cultural traditions and observations of nature.

items.title: Dhokra Metal Craft
items.explanation: The Dhokra craft is a 4000-year-old metal craft where a figure is made with clay, covered with wax, carved with details, then covered with more clay and fired. The wax melts and comes out of small openings when brass scrap is poured into the empty space.

items.title: Coconut Shell Craft
items.explanation: In coconut shell craft, a brown coconut shell is cleaned, smoothed, given a shape, fixed with a base, polished to shine, and used to make household things like bowls and jewellery. It is a biodegradable craft.

items.title: Kondapalli Toys
items.explanation: The Kondapalli art involves carving soft wood from hills, joining pieces with tamarind seed powder and sawdust paste, adding details, and finishing with vegetable dyes or enamel paints. These toys are based on folk stories, animals, birds, rural life, etc.

items.title: Art Order of Making
items.explanation: The order of making art forms is shown by specific words: to begin, first, then, after that, next, finally, at last. For example, in Dhokra, a figure is made with clay, then covered with wax, carved, and finally fired.

items.title: Present Tense Grammar
items.explanation: When children from different states speak about their art forms, they use the first form of the verb to show something that happens regularly. This is called the present tense, where -s/-es is used with he/she/it.

items.title: Gakkad Bharta Ingredients
items.explanation: To make gakkad bharta, balls of dough are made and cooked on high heat. Then brinjal and tomatoes are added, garnished with onions, coriander, green chillies, and salt. Finally, crumbled gakkad is served with ghee.

items.title: Madhubani Painting
items.explanation: Madhubani painting is a traditional art form from Bihar where artists use natural colours like haldi (yellow), leaves (green), red flowers/geru/sindoor (red), flowers (orange), and neel/indigo powder (blue) to paint on walls.
